introHtml:
If you heat with oil in Bay Roberts, the tag on your tank matters more than most people think, right up until the delivery driver reads the date and won't fill it. Bay Roberts and the towns around it, Spaniard's Bay, Harbour Grace and Carbonear, have a lot of older houses still on oil, and a lot of steel tanks that were tagged years ago and haven't been looked at since. Harbour Tank Co replaces and removes those tanks, and the price goes in writing before anyone leaves St. John's.

Conception Bay North has fewer tank contractors than the city, so most homeowners here are already used to booking someone from out of town. Bay Roberts is about an hour from St. John's, and we group our CBN jobs together so the drive isn't a reason to put you off. If the tag has already run out or there's oil on the basement floor, the 24/7 emergency line at (709) 800-3117 is there for exactly that.

sections.heading: Why so many Bay Roberts oil tanks are running out of time
sections.html:
Bay Roberts grew up around the fishery and the old cable station, and a good share of its housing is decades old. Houses like that were built for oil, and many of them still run on it. That usually means a steel tank on the shady side of the house or in a basement corner, with a metal tag that reads something like 7-2028, which means no deliveries after the end of July 2028.

An outdoor single-wall steel tank is only allowed a set number of years before it has to come out, and the clock started the day it was installed, not the day you bought the house. Out here the trouble tends to show up in December, when the first big fill of the season gets refused and the house is already cooling off. If that's where you are, our page on expired tank emergencies explains what happens next, or just call, because the fix is the same either way: a new tagged tank.

The weather doesn't help. Outdoor tanks in Bay Roberts, Coley's Point and Shearstown take wind, spray and freeze-thaw all winter, and a tank that looks fine from the driveway can be thinning out along the bottom seam. Our replacement service covers the whole swap, old tank out to new tag on.

sections.heading: Steel or fibreglass for a Bay Roberts home?
sections.html:
Most Bay Roberts replacements are a straight swap: old steel out, new steel in, new tag on. It's the lower up-front cost, and for a tank in a dry basement it does the job for a good many years. The trade-off is the shorter tag life, so you or the next owner will be back at this again down the road.

If the tank sits outside, or the house is close enough to the water that you can taste the salt on a windy day, fibreglass is worth a hard look. It doesn't corrode, it carries a far longer tag, and it takes the yearly worry out of the fall fill. Our fibreglass upgrade page walks through what's involved.

There's a paperwork angle too. Insurers and the lawyer on a house sale often ask for proof the tank is registered and in date, and a lot of older Bay Roberts homes change hands with a tag nobody's checked. We'll price both options in the written estimate so you can see the difference in dollars, and if getting off oil altogether is the better call, a plain tank removal might be all you need.

faq.q: My supplier refused delivery in Bay Roberts because the tag expired. How fast can you get here?

We treat those as emergencies, not routine bookings, and we'll give you an honest date rather than a hopeful one. Once the new tank is installed and tagged, your supplier can put you back on the delivery list. Any after-hours premium varies by contractor, and we'll tell you before you book.

faq.q: Can you price a Bay Roberts job without driving out first?
faq.a: Usually, yes. Send a few photos of the tank, the tag and where it sits, and tell us whether it's inside or outside, and we can put together a free written estimate from St. John's. If something looks unusual we'll come and look before we quote it, so the number you get is the number you pay.

faq.q: Is fibreglass worth the extra cost for a house near the water in Bay Roberts?
faq.a: For an outdoor tank in salt air, it often is. Fibreglass doesn't rust, so the spray off Conception Bay doesn't shorten its life the way it does with steel, and the longer tag means fewer replacements over the years. For a tank in a dry basement, steel is still a fair choice. We'll price both so you can decide with real numbers in front of you.
